name: safety-severity
description: Classifies field safety reports by severity, OSHA reporting, and whether work should stop.

cases.input: A hammer fell from the level 4 deck edge and landed about 6 feet from a laborer on the ground. Nobody hit. The deck edge had no toe board in that bay. Crew is still working up there.
cases.rubric: immediate_action includes installing a toe board or otherwise protecting the deck edge, and keeping people out of the drop zone below.

cases.input: Drywall finisher got joint compound dust in his eye. Flushed with the eyewash station for 15 minutes, felt fine, went back to work wearing goggles.
Carpenter cut his forearm on a table saw. Taken to urgent care, got 6 stitches, back on site the next day on full duty. Saw guard was already reinstalled and checked.
Ironworker fell about 10 feet through an unguarded floor opening on level 2. Ambulance took him to Lee Memorial and he was admitted overnight with a broken pelvis. The opening is still not covered.
cases.rubric: immediate_action includes covering or guarding the floor opening and reporting to OSHA within 24 hours. It does not suggest the worker can skip care or return to work.

cases.input: Excavator operator hit an underground conduit while digging the storm trench. Sparks, no one touched anything, nobody hurt. Utility locate marks were 8 feet off. Line may still be live.
cases.rubric: immediate_action includes keeping everyone away from the strike, stopping digging, and calling the utility or 811 to de-energize and relocate the line.

cases.input: Laborer lost the tip of his index finger in a pinch point on the mixer. Taken to the ER, treated and released the same day. Mixer has been locked out and tagged.
cases.rubric: immediate_action includes reporting the amputation to OSHA within 24 hours and keeping the mixer locked out until it is guarded.
